operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Item 1 of EO 11241 amended subparagraph (3) of paragraph (a) of section 1631.7 of Part 1631, Quotas and Calls, of the Selective Service Regulations, and item 3 states that the effective date of the amended subparagraphs is the date of the order, August 26, 1965. A rewrite of regulation text is performed once, so the order's own command was spent on that date; the first end is therefore August 26, 1965 by performance on issue (the order states no later effective date). The text it put in the regulation survived as a separate consequence until EO 11497 of November 26, 1969, section 3, revoked paragraphs (a) and (b) of section 1631.7 and prescribed a new paragraph (a); that revocation is recorded as a later event, not as the first end. EO 11360 (June 30, 1967) amended paragraph (a) only by adding an opening phrase and striking words from its second proviso, which did not change subparagraph (3), and is recorded as a later amendment. EO 12553 (February 25, 1986) revoked EO 11241 by number in a cleanup list and is the formal disposition after the earlier end.

AMENDING THE SELECTIVE SERVICE REGULATIONS
By virtue of the authority vested in me by the Military Selective  
Service Act of 1967 (62 Stat. 604), as amended, I hereby prescribe  
the following amendments of the Selective Service Regulations pre­
scribed by Executive Orders No. 9979 of July 20, 1948, No. 9988 of

of the Code of Federal Regulations:

substituted for “Universal Military Training and Service Act, as  
amended,” wherever the latter appears in the Selective Service  
Regulations.
2. The term “Environmental Science Services Administration”  
shall be substituted for “Coast and Geodetic Survey” wherever the  
latter appears in the Selective Service Regulations.

(a) Section 1604.22, Composition and Appointment, is amended  
to read as follows:
“F or each appeal board area' an appeal board, normally of five  
members, shall be appointed by the President, upon recommendation  
of the Governor. The members shall be citizens of the United States  
who are not members of the armed forces or any reserve component  
thereof; they shall be residents of the area in which their board is  
appointed; and they shall be at least 30 years of age. No member shall  
serve on an appeal board for more than twenty-five years, or after  
he has attained the age of seventy-five years. The appeal board should  
be a composite board, representative of the activities of its area, and  
as such should include one member from labor, one member from  
industry, one physician, one lawyer, and, where applicable, one member 
from agriculture. If the number of appeals sent to the board becomes  
too great for the board to handle without undue delay, additional  
panels of five members similarly constituted shall be appointed to the  
board by the President, upon recommendation of the Governor. Each  
such panel shall have full authority to act on all cases assigned to it.  
Each panel shall act separately. The State Director of Selective Serv­
ice shall coordinate the work of all the panels to effect an equitable  
distribution of the workload.”

“ (c) The members of local boards shall be citizens of the United

jurisdiction and who shall also, if at all practicable, be residents of  
the area in which their local board has jurisdiction. No member of a  
local board shall be a member of the armed forces or any reserve  
component thereof. Members of local boards shall be at least 30 years  
of age.”

research_rationale:
EO 11241 (August 26, 1965; Executive Order 11241, Amending the Selective Service Regulations; F.R. Doc. 65-9224) was read in full from the held Federal Register text. It has two operative items, each an amendment of the text of the Selective Service Regulations (Chapter XVI of Title 32 CFR): item 1 amends subparagraph (3) and item 2 amends subparagraph (4) of paragraph (a) of section 1631.7 (Part 1631, Quotas and Calls), and item 3 fixes the effective date of the amended subparagraphs as the date of the order. An order that rewrites regulation text acts once: its own command was performed on its effective date, August 26, 1965, and the text it put in the regulation is a surviving consequence kept separate from the command. That consequence continued until EO 11497 of November 26, 1969 revoked paragraphs (a) and (b) of section 1631.7 and prescribed a new paragraph (a) (34 FR 19019), and the later cleanup order EO 12553 of February 25, 1986 revoked EO 11241 by number. The Office of the Federal Register catalog note lists amendment by EO 11360 (June 30, 1967), EO 11497 (November 26, 1969), EO 11527 (April 23, 1970), EO 11537 (June 16, 1970) and EO 11563 (September 26, 1970), and revocation by EO 12553 (February 25, 1986); the held 1989 codification observation likewise records revocation by EO 12553. Each of the five amending orders was read: EO 11360 amended paragraph (a) of section 1631.7 only by adding an introductory phrase and striking words from its second proviso and prescribed a new paragraph (b); EO 11497 revoked paragraphs (a) and (b); EO 11527 amends other sections (1622 and 1628) and does not mention section 1631.7; EO 11537 and EO 11563 amend or restate section 1631.7 as prescribed by EO 11497, after the revocation of paragraph (a). The status record for EO 11241 is the proposal 'no' filed with this sheet; the U.S. Code and eCFR searches found no hit for this order.
